chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Red Nichols and the drummer he replaced, Vic Burton
summary: Morehouse calls Nichols a very good player, not a Bix imitator, and says Vic Burton, whom he replaced, was a much better drummer than he was.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Okay. Tell me, when you were with Red Nichols, you made a lot of records with Red Nichols.
Yeah.
Tell me about Red Nichols. What kind of a player was he?
Red Nichols was a very good player.
He sounded like Bix.
Yeah.
Did people think he was imitating Bix?
No, I don't think so.
Okay. Anything else about him as a leader? Do you remember anything about him?
No.
Okay. The drummer you replaced when you went with Red Nichols, the drummer was Vic Burton.
Vic Burton, yes.
Do you remember anything about him?
I remember he was a much better drummer than I was.
Oh he wasn't, was he? Was he really that good? Huh, was he really that good?
Yeah.
Then how come you replaced him? How come Red Nichols didn't keep him?
I don't know.
He came out of the Wolverines with Bix, if you remember. He was one of the Wolverines.
Yeah.
Bix played with him.
Yeah. I think that's it...
You think he was a very good drummer. Really? He didn't get the reputation that you had, for example. People don't know his name unless they're really dedicated jazz fans.
Yeah.
He didn't become as well known as some others.
Yeah.
I wonder why. Do you have any idea why?
No, I don't know why. Are these the pictures?
No. These are Red Nichols.
Red Nichols.
